title: Ptolemy's Inequality via Complex Numbers
description: Ptolemy's inequality proved using a simple algebraic identity over the complex numbers and the triangle inequality. For any four points in the plane: |z₁-z₃|·|z₂-z₄| ≤ |z₁-z₂|·|z₃-z₄| + |z₂-z₃|·|z₁-z₄|.

overview.historicalContext: Ptolemy's theorem, proved in the Almagest (c. 150 AD), states that for a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of opposite sides. The complex-number proof, popularized in Needham's Visual Complex Analysis and Aigner & Ziegler's Proofs from THE BOOK, reveals the theorem as a consequence of a simple ring identity.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Ptolemy's inequality for four points in the plane: $|z_1 - z_3| \cdot |z_2 - z_4| \leq |z_1 - z_2| \cdot |z_3 - z_4| + |z_2 - z_3| \cdot |z_1 - z_4|$.
overview.text: Ptolemy's inequality proved using complex numbers: the product of diagonals is at most the sum of products of opposite sides.
overview.proofStrategy: The proof has two steps: (1) establish the algebraic identity $(z_1-z_3)(z_2-z_4) = (z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4) + (z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)$ by ring expansion, then (2) take absolute values using the triangle inequality $|a+b| \leq |a|+|b|$ and multiplicativity $|ab|=|a||b|$.
keyInsights: Ptolemy's theorem is a consequence of a pure ring identity that holds in any commutative ring
The complex triangle inequality $|a+b| \leq |a|+|b|$ applied to the identity gives Ptolemy's inequality
Equality in Ptolemy's inequality characterizes concyclic points (points on a common circle)
This proof generalizes: the algebraic identity works over any commutative ring, and the inequality over any normed algebra

sections.title: The Algebraic Identity
sections.summary: Proves the fundamental ring identity $(z_1-z_3)(z_2-z_4) = (z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4) + (z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)$ using the `ring` tactic.
sections.mathContext: A pure algebraic identity over any commutative ring.

sections.title: Ptolemy's Inequality
sections.summary: Derives Ptolemy's inequality by taking absolute values of the algebraic identity and applying the complex triangle inequality $|a+b| \leq |a| + |b|$.
sections.mathContext: The triangle inequality transforms the algebraic identity into Ptolemy's metric inequality.

sections.title: Distance Formulation
sections.summary: Restates Ptolemy's inequality using the metric space distance function, connecting the complex-number proof to the standard geometric formulation.

conclusion.summary: This formalization demonstrates that Ptolemy's inequality is a natural consequence of complex number algebra. The proof is remarkably short: a one-line ring identity plus the triangle inequality.
conclusion.implications: The approach generalizes to normed algebras and reveals Ptolemy's theorem as fundamentally algebraic rather than geometric.
openQuestions: Can the equality case (concyclic points) be characterized purely algebraically?
Does the ring identity have analogues in higher-dimensional Clifford algebras?

crossReferences.description: Alternative proof of Ptolemy's theorem using complex numbers instead of Euclidean geometry
